# COMMUNITY ACQUIRED DIARRHEA (NO RECENT TRAVEL)

Most episodes of acute diarrhea are self-limited. In most mild to moderate cases, antimicrobial therapy does not provide benefit.
Acute diarrhea (< 14 days of symptoms)
Empirical antimicrobials should be given only in cases of severe acute disease or high-risk conditions: fever, >/= 6 stools in 24 hours, volume depletion requiring hospitalization, severe abdominal pain, immune compromise, cardiac disease, >/= 70 years old.
If in the preceding two months the patient has taken a PPI or has been hospitalized for three or more days, consider Clostridium difficile infection.
[Clostridium difficile](clostridiodes-difficile-infection)
Bloody diarrhea
Bloody diarrhea can represent hemorrhagic colitis or dysentery. Antimicrobial therapy and antimotility agents are not recommended in most patients with bloody diarrhea due to an increased risk of hemolytic uremic syndrome when using these agents. Obtain a stool sample for enteric pathogen PCR testing and reserve antimicrobial and antimotility agent treatment until results are known. For more information on when an antimicrobial is indicated or if the patient has severe/life threatening diarrhea or is immunocompromised, contact Infectious Diseases.

---

## Subacute or chronic (>/= 14 days of symptoms)

Primary treatment is hydration and electrolyte replacement. Empiric antimicrobial therapy is not indicated. Investigate for the cause of diarrhea.
Gastroenterology and/or Infectious Diseases involvement is encouraged.

Therapy:
## Primary treatment

Hydration and electrolyte replacement

## Empiric antimicrobial treatment (for severe disease or risk of severe disease)

Ciprofloxacin 500 mg PO q12h for 3-5 days [R,DI]
Alternative
Azithromycin 1000 mg PO one-time dose [M]
< OR >
Azithromycin 500 mg PO q24h for 3 days [M]
